openings.claim: Replace dependence on magnetic holding force with a serviceable mechanical pocket: mounting-slot-supported steel strips contact unmarked plate boundaries, overlapping lips resist lift, and a hinged keeper closes the removal route. Open the keeper and handle an unmarked plate area for inspection.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from magnetic attraction to geometric contact. Allocate three strips to fixed boundaries and the fourth to a pivoting keeper, using drilled strip holes, bolts, cork contact pads and a releasable wire latch. The keeper must remain attached during service.
openings.prediction: If the closed pocket has sufficiently small gaps and adequate stiffness, the spare plate stays within 1 mm through twenty strokes despite its weaker magnetic pull. The nearest rival, magnetic retention alone, instead depends on the supplied 3 N versus 7 N difference. Pocket drift should track gap or keeper deformation rather than magnetic pull strength; that relationship remains unmeasured.
openings.probe: First map slots, clearance, exposed edge and removal route with ruler and marker. Proceed only if M4 attachment, strip reach, formability and a gloved unmarked grip fit without modifying the plate or carriage. Use at most two configurations: magnets alone and the pocket. Observe one twenty-stroke run per plate per configuration, with the spare last. Mark initial positions and measure displacement; time one removal/return per plate, using gloves for the spare. Inspect keeper opening and strip deflection. Stay within eighty fabrication and twenty observation minutes and the supplied run/check caps; incomplete timed evidence does not qualify.
assumptions: Slot dimensions, strip stiffness/formability, available overlap outside clearance and safe grip access are unknown.
Defeat conditions include gaps or flex exceeding the displacement allowance, lift escaping the lips, keeper release, or gloved service exceeding sixty seconds.
Magnetic-rival failure is possible, not established; stroke forces are unknown.

assessment: A proposed probe, not deployment or demonstrated performance. Reject this fabrication if the initial geometry check cannot preserve every hard constraint; do not obtain fit by changing clearance, edge exposure or carriage attachment.
